exposure: restorative proctocolectomy (RPC) with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA)
surgical techniques (one- or modified two-stage RPC with stapled IPAA, fallopian tube traction technique)
mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
outcome: reasons for cesarean section (breech presentation, prior CS, rectovaginal fistula)
cohort: The study included 386 patients who underwent RPC with IPAA for UC between 2007 and 2023, with a focus on 83 females under 40 years of age for fertility and delivery outcomes.
finding: Fertility after RPC with IPAA appears to have improved, possibly due to the prevention of fallopian tube adhesions, and vaginal delivery is a feasible option after a stapled IPAA without a universal requirement for cesarean section.
mod_finding: After a stapled IPAA, vaginal delivery is a feasible option and cesarean section is not universally required solely because of the history of IPAA, with no significant differences in postpartum defecation between the vaginal delivery and cesarean section groups.
